newsitem.title: USA: Central Reserve sees Q3 loss beyond views.
newsitem.headline: Central Reserve sees Q3 loss beyond views.

text.p: Central Reserve Life Corp said Tuesday it expects to report a loss of $0.40 to $0.45 per share for the third quarter that ended September 30, 1996.
First Call analysts' estimates called for a loss of $0.05 per share.

"Our strategy for returning to profitability is as aggressive as we can implement at this time without losing existing business or losing the opportunity to gain our share of new business," said Fred Lick, Central Reserve Life's chairman, in a statement accompanying the announcement.

"Although we are showing a loss for the third quarter, we are pleased with the improving trend. As previously announced, we implemented the most aggressive rate adjustments possible on April 1, 1996, for all new business and all renewal accounts.

"These rate increases have only affected 50 percent of our renewal accounts (April 1996 through September 1996), and by the time we finish the twelve-month renewal cycle at the end of the first quarter of 1997, we should return to the type of profitability posture that we have enjoyed in prior years," he said.
The company said it expects to report full financial results for the third quarter on November 12.
